steps.title: Assemble well‑plate electrode
steps.instruction: Construct the electrode‑integrated well plate by aligning PCBs with double‑sided adhesive tape and inserting Au‑coated pins.

substeps.instruction: Place the bottom PCB face‑up on a flat surface and lay double‑sided adhesive tape over it.
Cut the tape around the PCB edges with a razor blade so the tape matches the PCB dimensions.
Place the top PCB on the tape and use it as a stencil to mark well locations with a marker.
Cut holes at the markings using a plotter cutter or a 10–15 mm biopsy punch.
Insert a razor blade at a corner of the tape, peel off one side of the protective film, and remove it with tweezers.
Position the bottom PCB (pads facing up) adjacent to the tape; align the tape holes concentric to the Au pads on the PCB.
Press the tape firmly onto the bottom PCB using a rigid cylinder to roll over the adhesive film and create a tight seal.
Remove the remaining protective film from the tape by sliding a razor blade under it and lifting the laminate with tweezers.
Place the bottomless well plate on the taped bottom PCB, align the wells with the Au pads, and press firmly to seal.
Insert the push‑fit receptacles into the holes of the top PCB and insert the Au‑coated pins into the receptacles.
Solder the pin headers to the top PCB to connect the assembly to the function generator.

steps.title: Fabricate localized electroporation devices
steps.instruction: Build individual LEPD units by combining glass cloning cylinders, a track‑etched polycarbonate membrane, and double‑sided adhesive tape.

substeps.instruction: Sonicate glass cloning cylinders in acetone for 10 min, then rinse with ethanol and deionized distilled water (DDW) and dry with N₂ gas.
Punch ~10 holes (6 mm diameter) in double‑sided adhesive tape to cover a 75 mm × 25 mm area.
Peel off one side of the protective film from the tape using a razor blade at a corner and remove the laminate with tweezers.
Place a track‑etched polycarbonate membrane on a clean glass slide and treat it in an oxygen plasma cleaner for 5 min.
Lay the membrane onto the sticky side of the tape, keeping it flat with the rigid microscope slide as support.
Flip the membrane‑tape assembly and remove the remaining protective film with a razor blade and tweezers.
Position a cloning cylinder on each pre‑cut hole of the exposed adhesive side and press down to activate the pressure‑adhesive tape, ensuring a tight seal.
Repeat the press step for every hole in the tape.
Cut the tape with scissors to separate each cylinder‑tape‑membrane unit and trim excess tape around each cylinder.
Spray the scissors with 70 % ethanol in DI water to prevent tape adhesion.
Place the completed devices in a well‑plate dish and expose them to UV light for 4 h.

steps.title: Treat surfaces and prepare cell culture
steps.instruction: Coat LEPD membranes with fibronectin and prepare complete growth medium for HeLa cells.

substeps.instruction: Dilute fibronectin stock (0.1 % solution) 20 µL into 1 mL PBS to obtain 20 µg/mL.
Add 100 µL of this fibronectin solution to each LEPD, incubate 1 h at room temperature in a biosafety cabinet.
Discard excess solution and wash each LEPD twice with 100 µL PBS.
Prepare complete DMEM medium: mix 449 mL DMEM, 50 mL FBS (10 % v/v), and 1 mL Pen‑Strep (1 % v/v).

steps.title: Seed and culture HeLa cells on devices
steps.instruction: Grow HeLa cells to confluence, detach, and seed them onto the fibronectin‑coated LEPDs.

substeps.instruction: Seed HeLa cells at 3 × 10⁵ cells per well in 6‑well plates using 2 mL complete medium per well.
Incubate until confluence is reached (~1 × 10⁶ cells per well).
Remove medium, add 1 mL warm (37 °C) trypsin‑EDTA to each well, and incubate 5 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Gently pipette to detach cells, transfer the suspension to a 15 mL Falcon tube, and add 4 mL complete medium to neutralize trypsin.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL fresh complete medium.
Count cells and dilute to a concentration of 200 cells/µL.
Add 100 µL (20 000 cells) of the suspension to each LEPD.
Add an additional 100 µL of complete medium to each well.
Incubate the LEPDs overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to allow cell adhesion.

steps.title: Prepare suspension cells for electroporation
steps.instruction: Harvest, count, and load suspension cells into LEPDs with electroporation buffer.

substeps.instruction: Verify cell viability and determine cell density using a hemocytometer or automated counter.
Aliquot enough cells to obtain 30 000–50 000 cells per device (e.g., ~1.2 × 10⁶ cells for 24 devices).
Transfer the cell suspension to a Falcon tube, balance the tube, and centrifuge at 150 × g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant, add electroporation buffer (100 µL per device; 2.4 mL total for 24 devices), and resuspend the pellet.
Dispense 100 µL of the cell‑buffer mixture into each LEPD placed in a well plate.
Place the plate in a centrifuge with a counterweight plate (≈200 µL fluid per well) opposite the devices and centrifuge at 150 × g for 5 min.

steps.title: Optimize plasmid delivery parameters
steps.instruction: Load eGFP plasmid onto electrodes, apply bi‑level pulses, and recover cells.

substeps.instruction: Prepare eGFP plasmid solutions at 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, and 350 ng/µL (minimum 5 µL each).
Remove electroporation buffer from each LEPD and add 200 µL fresh buffer; let the buffer equilibrate to room temperature.
If using non‑adherent cells, centrifuge the LEPDs at 150 × g for 5 min.
Using a sterile tweezer, place a 5 µL droplet of the appropriate plasmid concentration onto the bottom gold electrode of each column (column 1 = 100 ng/µL, … column 6 = 350 ng/µL).
Place each LEPD onto a well containing its plasmid droplet (one LEPD per well).
Set the pulse program to a bi‑level waveform: V₁ = 10–40 V (varied), V₂ = 10 V, T₁ = 0.5 ms, T₂ = 0.5–2.5 ms, frequency = 20 Hz, pulse count = 100–800.
Connect the positive terminal of the power box to the top plate row 1 and the negative terminal to the bottom plate.
Check system resistance with the Infinitesimal software; ensure a stable 1–2 MΩ reading.
Apply the pulse sequence (≈2 min). After completion, switch the positive terminal to the next row and repeat for all four rows.
When all rows have been pulsed, disconnect the power, lift the top plate, and transfer the LEPDs to a new transparent well plate.
Remove electroporation buffer, add fresh complete culture medium to each LEPD, and return the plate to the incubator.

steps.title: Automated imaging of transfected cells
steps.instruction: Stain nuclei, acquire fluorescence images, and process data using a motorized microscope.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 12‑well plate with 1 mL PBS in each well.
Dip each LEPD sequentially into three wells (do not fully submerge) to rinse the membrane surface, then place the devices into a transparent 24‑well imaging plate.
Make a Hoechst 33342 staining solution (0.1 mg/mL in PBS).
Aspirate any fluid from each well, add 100 µL Hoechst solution, and incubate 10 min.
Aspirate the Hoechst solution, wash the wells three times with PBS, and add 150 µL PBS for imaging.
Mount the plate on a motorized microscope stage.
Program the stage to move to the centre of each well; use a 10× or 20× objective with a DAPI filter to capture images of stained nuclei.
Focus manually on the first well or use an autofocus routine that selects the Z‑plane with the highest focus score.
Acquire images with the required fluorescence and bright‑field filters for each field of view; obtain multiple fields per LEPD as needed.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol or parts of it has been used and validated in the following research article(s): Patino et al. [9]. Multiplexed high-throughput localized electroporation workflow with deep learning–based analysis for cell engineering. Sci Adv. (Figures 4–7).
